question: A team is deciding whether to delegate a large, one-off dependency-audit task to a subagent instead of running it in the main conversation. The audit will read many files and produce a lot of intermediate output that won't be needed again after a summary is produced. Which of the following are genuine benefits of using a subagent for this task? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) The verbose intermediate output stays in the subagent's own context window, keeping the main conversation's context free for other work.
B) The subagent can be restricted to a specific tool allowlist, such as read-only tools, so it can't accidentally modify files during the audit.
C) Delegating to a subagent automatically skips all permission prompts for every tool the subagent uses, regardless of configuration.
D) The subagent can be configured to run on a cheaper, faster model than the main conversation if the audit doesn't need the most capable model.
E) Delegating to a subagent guarantees the audit finishes faster than running the same steps in the main conversation.
correct_answers: A) The verbose intermediate output stays in the subagent's own context window, keeping the main conversation's context free for other work.
B) The subagent can be restricted to a specific tool allowlist, such as read-only tools, so it can't accidentally modify files during the audit.
D) The subagent can be configured to run on a cheaper, faster model than the main conversation if the audit doesn't need the most capable model.
explanations: Correct -- this is a core benefit: verbose exploration and intermediate output stay in the subagent's own context, and only the relevant summary returns to the main conversation.
Correct -- a subagent's tools field can be set as an allowlist, letting the team restrict it to read-only tools and enforce that it can't modify files.
Incorrect -- permission behavior still depends on the configured permission mode; delegation to a subagent doesn't automatically bypass every prompt.
Correct -- a subagent's model can be configured independently of the main conversation, so a lower-cost model can be used when the task doesn't need the most capable one.
Incorrect -- subagents start with fresh context and can take time gathering that context, so delegation doesn't guarantee a faster finish than working in the main conversation.
